auth.cli.usage:
Manage Ho!! accounts:

  add <name> [password]     create an account; without a password one is rolled
  del <name>                delete an account
  passwd <name> [password]  reset a password
  name <name> <spelling>    set how the name is shown, e.g. BATMAN
  list                      show accounts

Accounts live in {file}. Only the name and a scrypt hash are stored, never a
password in the clear. Passwords are at least {n} characters long.
auth.cli.passwordHint: Pass it on to the player; on the first sign-in they have to choose their own.
auth.cli.mustChangeHint: On the next sign-in a new password has to be chosen.
auth.cli.deletedHint: Open sessions of that account end right away.
auth.cli.none: No accounts yet. Create one with: add <name>
auth.cli.badSpelling: The spelling must be the same name, only with different upper/lower case.
auth.cli.badName: Invalid name. Allowed are 2 to 24 characters from a-z, 0-9, dot, minus and underscore.

shipinfo.hint: Click a ship to see its profile.
ship.scout.info: The fastest type, with a long range. Scouts explore new worlds – only then do you learn their temperature, gravity and ore. They cannot fight and barely take a hit, so steer clear of enemy fleets.
ship.fighter.info: Carries weapons and shields and conquers worlds: whoever holds the orbit and breaks the defences and satellites takes the world. Its range is short – send a tanker along for strikes deep in enemy space.
ship.satellite.info: Placed straight into orbit of the world that builds it and stays there. Cheap, tough and well armed – ideal for guarding border worlds. Counts as presence in orbit: a world with satellites does not fall without a fight.
ship.colony.info: Flies to a free world and lands 8M settlers there; the ship is used up. Over one of your own worlds that is not yet full, “Drop settlers here” tops up the population. Slow and defenceless – an escort pays off.
ship.tanker.info: Does not fight, but gives the whole fleet its range – more than twice that of a fighter. Every additional tanker in the same fleet adds +15%. Merge it with fighters or colony ships using “Merge fleets” to reach distant targets.

help.title: How to play Ho!!
help.goal.p: Settle worlds, build fleets and be the last empire standing. Everyone moves at the same time: you give your orders and click End turn. Once everyone is done, the server resolves the turn.
help.worlds.p: The colour shows the temperature (blue = icy, red = scorching), the size shows gravity. The closer a world is to the ideal (20 °C, 1.0 g), the more people live there – and the more money it brings in. A genuinely habitable world looks the part, too: oceans, green continents and polar caps. The temperature then shows in the colour of the continents – an ice world is blue as well, but bare. The ore bar shows the metal reserve; metal is consumed as it is mined. Once it is empty, the world still yields a tenth through deep mining.
help.rings.p: The solid ring carries the colour of its empire. A dashed circle marks a homeworld. Four yellow brackets mean: currently selected. What orbits the world as a symbol are its satellites (from five on, the number is shown next to it).
help.terra.p: With money you push temperature and gravity towards the ideal. Extreme worlds need radical tech first.
help.research.p: You decide which share of your income goes into research and how it is split across six fields. Ships are built with the tech level that applies at build time. Older ships can be refitted for a surcharge in orbit of one of your own shipyards.
help.space.p: On the Space playing field the worlds lie in a lens rather than on a disc. Drag rotates the camera, Shift+drag pans it, the mouse wheel zooms. A plumb line from every world down to the grid shows its height; T switches to top-down view, F fits the whole galaxy.
help.fleets.p: Click a fleet, then click the target world. The fleet travels as far as its slowest ship allows. Range measures the distance from your nearest inhabited world – tankers extend it.
help.combat.p: When hostile ships meet at a world, they fight. Whoever holds the orbit and finds no defence left conquers the world. Satellites are cheap defenders and never leave home.
